messages.content: i usually walk to the library, but today i stayed home. the afternoon feels long without the walk.
the walk may be part of how you move from one part of your day to another. would you like to do something small at home, or just talk for a while?
just talk. i did read at home, so i had time with the book. i think i wanted the journey too.
then the walk gives you something different from the reading. you can enjoy getting to a place as well as what you do when you get there.
i like seeing which people are outside. sometimes the same person is near the same tree.
those little things can become part of a place you know. even when you do not stop to talk, you see a part of other people going through their day.
can you write what i said in three sentences, without adding a reason i did not give?
i usually walk to the library, but today i stayed home. i read at home, so i had time with the book. i still wanted the journey and seeing people outside.
now make it sound more like a message to a friend.
i read at home today, but i wanted my walk to the library too. i like seeing people outside along the way.
tell me a story about someone finding a message they wrote for themselves and forgot about.

a woman opens an old book while looking for a picture. between the pages, she finds a note in her own writing. it says: ask your aunt about the garden. she can remember that she wanted to know how the garden began, but she never asked. the aunt still lives in the same house, so the woman calls her. they talk about the tree near the door and the flowers that used to grow by the wall. the note did not give her the answer. it brought back a question she still wanted to ask.
tell the part about her memory simply.
she wanted to know how the garden began, but she never asked. now she can remember that question.
did the note tell her the whole story of the garden?
no. it gave her a question. she learned more by calling her aunt and talking with her.
what could she write on a new note after the call?
i asked my aunt about the garden. the tree by the door and the flowers by the wall are part of its story. i want to write down what she told me.
why not write that her aunt put every flower in the garden?
the story did not say who put them there. the new note should keep to what was given.
someone stood up from a chair near me. i want to sit there, but i do not know whether they are coming back. what can i ask?
are you finished with this chair, or will you be coming back?
they say they are just getting a book. what does that tell me?
it gives you a reason for them to stand up. they may still want the chair. if you are not sure, ask whether they are keeping it.
write a question asking whether i can sit there.
may i sit here, or are you coming back to this chair?
make it shorter.
are you keeping this chair?
now ask only whether i can use it.
may i use this chair?
they say i can use it because they will read at another table. write my reply.
thank you. i will sit here, then. enjoy your book.
here is a story: my mother found my book, and i said thank you to her. change it so my brother is the one who found it, but i still thank the person who helped.
my brother found my book, and i said thank you to him.
now make it about both my mother and brother finding it together.
my mother and brother found my book, and i said thank you to them.
what changed when you used them?
them is about both people in that sentence. you said thank you to your mother and your brother, rather than only one of them.
now let my brother find the book while my mother is in the kitchen. keep the thanks only for my brother.
my brother found my book while my mother was in the kitchen, and i said thank you to him.
does being in the kitchen mean my mother did not help in any other way?
no. that detail only says where she was then. it does not tell us everything she did before or after that moment.
can you leave that open rather than saying she did nothing?
yes. the sentence can say that your brother found the book and your mother was in the kitchen. it does not need to add that she did nothing.
in my made up town, the library is east of the park. the shop is west of the park. which place is in the middle of those two?
with those three places on one east to west line, the park is in the middle. the shop is to its west, and the library is to its east.
give the answer in fewer words.
the park is between the shop and the library.
can i say the shop is east of the library?
no. with the places as you gave them, the shop is west of the library.
write a small journey from the shop to the library that goes past the park.
a girl leaves the shop and goes east along the road. she goes past the park, then keeps going until she comes to the library. she stops there to return a book.
tell the journey in fewer words.
a girl leaves the shop and goes east past the park. she stops at the library to return a book.
where did she start?
she started at the shop, west of the park.
my friend said not now when i asked to talk. i want to give them time without making the whole conversation feel over.
you could say: okay. tell me when you have time, and we can talk then.
i do not want them to feel they must choose a time right away.
then leave that part open: okay. we do not have to choose a time now. i would still like to talk when you are ready.
what if i need an answer about a plan before tomorrow?
then you can make that need clear without asking for a long conversation: i need to know about tomorrow before the end of today. could you send a short answer when you can?
can you keep the request about a plan, not about their feelings?
i need to know whether our plan for tomorrow still works. could you send a short answer before the end of today?
if they say no, what would be a simple reply?
thanks for telling me. we can choose another day if you would like to.
does that say for sure we will make a new plan?
no. it leaves room for another plan if both people want one. it does not say that a new day has already been chosen.
write a story about a grandfather drawing the house where he lived as a child. let someone ask about a detail he does not remember.

a grandfather draws a small house on a page. his daughter asks why there is no color on the door. he says that he can remember the door being large, but he does not remember its color. she asks whether he could make it blue. he says he could choose blue for a picture, but that would not mean the old door really was blue. they leave the door white and draw the tree that he can remember next to the wall.
keep just the part about what he can remember.
he says that he can remember the door being large, but he does not remember its color. they leave the door white and draw the tree that he can remember next to the wall.
what is the difference between choosing blue and knowing the old door was blue?
he can choose blue for the picture without knowing that the old door was blue. choosing a color does not make it a fact about the old house.
make that answer simple.
he can choose blue now even if he does not know the color of the old door.
write a short note that could go under the drawing.
the house where i lived as a child. some details are clear in my memory, and some are not.
i asked two friends to bring a book, but only one heard me. can i say both knew what i wanted?
not from that fact alone. one heard your request. the other might learn it another way, but you have not said that happened.
one friend told the other later. now can both know?
yes. one friend can hear your request and then tell the other. both can know what you wanted, even if only one heard you ask.
say that in fewer words.
yes. one friend can tell the other what you asked.
write a short story with that order.
i asked two friends to bring a book. only one heard me at first. later, that friend told the other what i had asked. when we met, they both knew about the request.
did both have to bring a different book?
not from your words alone. bring a book could be about one book between them or one from each person. you can ask if you need that detail to be clear.
ask a question to make it clear.
do you want one book from each of us, or one book for us to bring together?
i have a holiday tomorrow and no plans. usually i feel i should have a task for every hour of the day.
you can leave some time open. having a day free does not mean every hour has to become a task.
i think i need a task for every hour. can you say it simply?
you do not need to choose something for every hour. you can plan one thing you want and leave the rest of the day open.
i want to go to the library, but i do not want to choose a time yet.
then the plan can stay general: visit the library if you feel like it tomorrow. you can choose the hour later.
i want the visit to be a real plan, not just something i might do.
then write: go to the library tomorrow. choose the time in the morning. that keeps the visit in the plan while leaving the hour open for now.
what if i want a quiet morning at home first?
you can plan that too: have a quiet morning at home, then choose a time to visit the library later in the day.
does that mean i must read the whole afternoon?
no. visiting the library does not choose how long you stay or how much you read.
i found a note from yesterday and a note from last month. both say bring the book. do they have to be about the same book?
no. the same words can be used to ask for different things. you need context to know which book each note is about.
both are from my sister. does that tell us which book she wanted?
no. your sister can ask about different books on different days. knowing who wrote each note still does not tell us which book it is about.
explain simply.
your sister could want a different book on each day. the words alone do not tell us.
what could i ask her about yesterday?
which book did you want yesterday when you wrote bring the book?
use are you asking for instead of did you want.
which book are you asking for in the note from yesterday?
make that question shorter.
which book is your note from yesterday about?
in my story, a child talks to a plant every morning. write a quiet first part without saying whether the plant can answer.

a child sits near a plant by the window. each morning, she talks about one thing with it about the day before. sometimes she talks about school, and sometimes she reads a line from her book. the plant gives no answer, but she likes having that little time before breakfast. one day, her brother can hear her and asks who she is talking to. she says that she is telling the plant about her day.
make the part about her brother past rather than now.
one day, her brother heard her and asked who she was talking to. she said that she was telling the plant about her day.
does the story say that every plant can understand words?
no. the child talks to the plant, but the story does not say that it can understand her words.
say that in fewer words.
no. the story says that she talks to it, not that it can understand.
now add one sentence where the brother wants to join without making the plant talk.
he sits next to her and asks whether he can tell the plant about his day too.
my friend is telling me how to play a game, but there is too much information at once. i want the basic idea first.
you could say: can you give me the basic idea first? then i can ask about the other parts one at a time.
say my first sentence simply.
my friend is telling me how to play a game, but there is too much information at once.
i do not want to say they are wrong to teach it that way.
you do not need to. keep it about what helps you learn: i learn better when i start with one simple part. could we do that first?
can you give a reply using only the request?
could we start with one simple part of the game, please?
they ask which part. i do not know the game well enough to choose.
you can ask them to choose the first thing a new person needs to know: what should i learn before trying the first part?
can i ask them to show one example?
yes. you could say: could you show me one example before telling me more?
my neighbor gave me food in a container. i finished the food and want to return the container. help me write a note.
thank you for the food. i would like to return your container. when would be a good time?
i will leave the container by her door after she said that was okay. i do not need to ask when.
thank you for the food. i will leave your container by the door, as you said i could.
keep the message but ask for nothing else.
thank you for the food. i will leave your container by the door, as you said i could.
by the time she reads it, it will be there. can the note say i have left it?
yes. if the note is with the container, it can say that you have left it there.
keep just yes and the message.
yes. i have left your container by the door, as you said i could.
write the note without adding anything about the taste of the food.
thank you for the food. i have left your container by the door, as you said i could.
two people look at the same picture. one talks about the tree, and the other talks about the house. are they talking about different pictures?
not always. a picture can have both a tree and a house. each person may be talking about a different part of the same picture.
say it simply.
no. they can be talking about different parts of the same picture.
write a short conversation with both details.
i like the tree on the left. i was looking at the house. do you see the little window? yes, and the tree is right next to it. i had not looked at that part yet.
does the person who likes the tree have to hate the house?
no. the person only said that they like the tree. they did not tell us how they feel about the house.
make that answer simple.
no. a person can like both parts, even when they only talk about one.
what could they ask each other next?
what else do you like in the picture?
write a short story about an animal leaving a room and coming back. keep the animal the same one through the whole story.

a small animal sat under a table while a child read. after a while, it walked through the open door into the garden. the child kept reading until she heard a sound near the door. the same animal came back and sat under the table again. she looked down, then turned another page and went on with the story.
write that in fewer words.
a child read while an animal sat under the table. it went into the garden, then came back and sat in the same place. the child saw it return and kept reading.
why is the same animal an important detail?
it is the animal that left, rather than a new animal coming in.
say that using it came back.
it came back, so it is the same animal that left.
i asked my cousin if she wants a book, and she has not answered. is that the same as saying no?
no. not answering yet does not give a yes or a no. she may not have read the message or may need time to think.
i need to know before i go to the shop tomorrow. help me ask once more.
could you let me know before tomorrow whether you want the book? i am going to the shop then.
i am going tomorrow afternoon, not tomorrow morning. can i give her more time?
yes. you can ask for an answer before you leave tomorrow afternoon, rather than before the start of tomorrow.
write the message itself.
could you tell me before tomorrow afternoon whether you want the book? i need to know before i go to the shop.
what if she still does not reply?
you will need to choose what to do without knowing her answer. you can tell her your plan rather than saying she said no when she did not.
give me a message if i choose not to buy it without an answer.
i did not hear back before leaving, so i did not buy the book. we can talk about it another day.
